symptom: `drop user role Spare` passed check and exec while a retrieve and an access rule still named the role by its XPath token '[%UserRole_Spare%]'; mx check then reported CE1613 "The selected user role 'Spare' no longer exists." at both.
cause: execDropUserRole and check's grant resolver refused a drop only while the administrator role or a demo user held the role. A token is a string inside an XPath, so no typed reader and no reference edge saw it.
fix: Both scan every stored unit's bytes for the exact token (case-sensitive, as mxbuild matches it; the closing %] keeps SpareTwo from naming Spare) and refuse, naming each document. check skips documents a statement above created or dropped, so `drop microflow …; drop user role …` passes as exec does.
insight: A byte search over ListRawUnitsByType("") is the right instrument for a token: it reaches access rules in domain models, which the member-ref walker excludes on purpose. Measured on 11.12.6 with the pre-fix binary: the drop gives exactly two CE1613 — at the access rule and at the retrieve — the two places the refusal now names.
test: mdl/executor/security_drop_role_token_2529_test.go (refused; clean order passes; a token naming SpareTwo does not hold Spare)
